title: Groups of Special-Equivalent Strings
summary: Given an array of strings of equal length, determine the number of groups where each group consists of strings that can be made identical through any number of swaps of characters at even or odd indices.
statement: Given an array of strings of equal length, determine the number of groups where each group consists of strings that can be made identical through any number of swaps of characters at even or odd indices. Each group must be the largest possible set of special-equivalent strings.
constraints: Swaps may occur between indices with the same parity.
Count equivalence groups under arbitrary even-even and odd-odd swaps.
reference_solution:
def special_equivalent_group_count(words):
 return len({(''.join(sorted(word[::2])),''.join(sorted(word[1::2]))) for word in words})
hints: Same-parity swaps can arbitrarily permute even positions and odd positions independently.
Use sorted even-index and sorted odd-index characters as a canonical key.
The key is invariant under allowed swaps and equal keys can be transformed by parity-wise permutations.
editorial: The key is invariant under allowed swaps and equal keys can be transformed by parity-wise permutations.

tests.explanation: The words form three parity-multiset groups.
The six permutations form three special-equivalence groups.
